name: Kozilek's Command
notes: The ability's text is the 'Choose two' line alone: a modal bullet is not a line of its own (README, Claiming lines), and naming all four bullets would put the ability over its budget - a choose-mode counts once per substantive mode, so four modes cannot pay for five named lines. The Spawn token's 'Sacrifice this token: Add {C}.' is the token op's spawn flag. lint bug workaround: the token's count is written as {sum:['X']} and the graveyard-card target carries an empty filter, because src/cards/lint.ts rejects a literal Amount / TargetSpec count of 'X' as an 'unknown amount count' unless a sibling `filter` is present.

issues: • Exile target creature with mana value X or less. — expected With X=2 paid, any creature of mana value 2 or less is a legal target and the mode is offerable. — scripted {op:'exile', target:{kind:'creature', filter:{mvLE:'X'}}}. src/engine/characteristics.ts:260 evaluates a non-numeric mvLE via evalAmount(s, f.mvLE, ctrl, 0, source) — the x argument is HARDCODED 0, so 'X' always evaluates to 0 and the filter means 'mana value 0 or less'. The blind scenario confirms it: with x:2 against an mv-2 creature the engine offered only mode combos 1+2, 1+4, 2+4 — mode 3 is never legal against any creature with mv>=1. The mode is effectively dead text. — CR CR 601.2b (X is locked in as the value chosen while casting) / CR 115.1

• Target player creates X 0/1 colorless Eldrazi Spawn creature tokens with "Sacrifice this token: Add {C}." — expected Tokens named "Eldrazi Spawn". — scripted The token op carries no `name`, so game.ts:1332 derives the name as `${subtypes.join(' ')} token` = "Eldrazi Spawn token". Cosmetic in the engine (render.ts:594 prints 'Eldrazi Spawn' off the spawn flag), but the token object is built from src.def, so its def.name is "Kozilek's Command" — the scenario harness's findByName (scenarioDsl.ts:418) searches def.name and cannot see an 'Eldrazi Spawn'. Adding name:'Eldrazi Spawn' fixes the printed name; the def.name collision is a harness limitation, not a script defect. — CR CR 111.4

Choose two — / all four bullets — expected Each printed bullet accounted for by a claimed line or an explicit `covers`/`ignore` entry. — scripted The single ability's `text` is "Choose two —" alone and the script has no `covers` block; the four mode bullets are unclaimed. The notes argue a budget rule permits this, but as written nothing in the script file claims the bullet text, so the modes' correctness (including the dead mode 3) is invisible to line-level checking. — CR CR 700.2

• Exile up to X target cards from graveyards. — expected Up to X cards, chosen from ANY player's graveyard. — scripted target {kind:'graveyard-card', count:'X', optional:true, filter:{}} with no `who` — legal.ts:153 then scans every player's graveyard, and `optional` gives 'up to'. This clause is correct; recorded only to note that the empty `filter` is a lint workaround, not a semantic restriction.

• Exile target creature with mana value X or less. — expected a creature whose mana value is <= the X paid for the spell is a legal target (X=2 -> mana value 2 legal) — scripted exile target {kind:'creature', filter:{mvLE:'X'}} — src/engine/characteristics.ts:260 evaluates a filter's mvLE with evalAmount(..., 0, ...): the item's X is hard-coded to 0, so the filter is 'mana value 0 or less'. Blind scenario 3 confirms: with x:2 and a mana-value-2 Grizzly Bears on the battlefield the mode is never offered ('no legal action matched'; only mode pairs 1+2, 1+4, 2+4 exist). Mode 3 is effectively unplayable. — CR 115.1 / 202.3

• Target player creates X 0/1 colorless Eldrazi Spawn creature tokens with "Sacrifice this token: Add {C}." — expected the created objects are named 'Eldrazi Spawn' — scripted token op omits `name`, so token.name defaults to 'Eldrazi Spawn token' and the object's def stays the source card, so def.name is "Kozilek's Command". Scenarios 1 and 5 fail on that name ('Eldrazi Spawn not found'). Behaviourally the spawn mana ability and 0/1 colorless body are right (mana.ts:32, game.ts:1332), so this is a naming/harness-level defect, not a rules error; an explicit `name: "Eldrazi Spawn"` would remove it. — CR 111.4

• Target player scries X, then draws a card. — expected target player scries X and that same player draws — scripted correct — scoped who:'target-player' rebinds item.actor, and both scry and draw who:'you' resolve to the scoped player (game.ts:1017, 1575); scenario 2 passes — CR 121.1

• Exile up to X target cards from graveyards. — expected up to X target cards in ANY graveyard — scripted correct — graveyard-card spec with no `who` scans every player's graveyard (legal.ts:153, types.ts:41), count 'X' via specCount, optional true; scenario 4 passes — CR 701.19a
